extracted.intended_audience: users and developers who want to install, run, or contribute to the 3b1b/manim (ManimGL) repository (3Blue1Brown users, animation authors, Python developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for installing, running, configuring, and contributing to the 3b1b/manim (ManimGL) animation engine, including platform-specific steps, dependencies, CLI usage, and contributing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version selection: ManimGL vs Manim Community
rubrics_metrics.description: WARNING: These instructions are for ManimGL only. Trying to use these instructions to install Manim Community/manim or instructions there to install this version will cause problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide which version you wish to install, then only follow the instructions for your desired version. The repository began as 3Blue1Brown's personal project; a separate community edition fork exists with different goals and installation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package name for pip installation
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: To install manim directly through pip, please pay attention to the name of the installed package. This repository is ManimGL of 3b1b. The package name is manimgl instead of manim or manimlib. Please use pip install manimgl to install the version in this repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the wrong package name (e.g., pip install manim) will install a different project/version and cause incompatibilities. For development installs from the cloned repo, use pip install -e .

rubrics_metrics.name: Python version requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Manim runs on Python 3.7 or higher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your environment uses Python >= 3.7; some install instructions/examples reference Python 3.9 for conda environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core system dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: System requirements are FFmpeg, OpenGL and LaTeX (optional, if you want to use LaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install FFmpeg and ensure OpenGL is available on your system. LaTeX is only required for rendering TeX/LaTeX in scenes. Missing FFmpeg or OpenGL will prevent rendering/exporting animations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linux additional dependency: Pango development headers
rubrics_metrics.description: For Linux, Pango along with its development headers are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the linked Linux instructions for installing Pango and its dev headers to avoid missing-symbol errors when rendering text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Windows installation: FFmpeg, LaTeX recommended (MiKTeX), and dev install steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Directly (Windows): Install FFmpeg. Install a LaTeX distribution. MiKTeX is recommended. Install the remaining Python packages. git clone https://github.com/3b1b/manim.git cd manim pip install -e . manimgl example_scenes.py OpeningManimExample
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these steps in order; MiKTeX is recommended for LaTeX. After pip install -e ., test the install by running an example scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mac OSX installation notes and lightweight LaTeX alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Mac OSX: Install FFmpeg, LaTeX in terminal using homebrew. brew install ffmpeg mactex. An alternative to heavyweight MacTeX bundle: BasicTeX to avoid installing ~6GB, then add only necessary LaTeX packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using an ARM-based Mac, install Cairo: arch -arm64 brew install pkg-config cairo. For cloned-repo development installs, git clone and pip install -e ., then run example scenes; on ARM ensure manimgl is on your PATH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anaconda installation workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Anaconda Install: Install LaTeX as above. Create a conda environment using conda create -n manim python=3.9. Activate the environment using conda activate manim. Install manimgl using pip install -e .
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a dedicated conda environment (example uses Python 3.9). Ensure LaTeX and FFmpeg are available in the system or environment before running examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development install workflow (hacking on manimlib)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to hack on manimlib itself, clone this repository and in that directory execute: pip install -e .
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After editable install, run an example to verify the development install: manimgl example_scenes.py OpeningManimExample or manim-render example_scenes.py OpeningManimExample. Include manimgl on your PATH if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify installation by running example scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Try running the following: manimgl example_scenes.py OpeningManimExample — This should pop up a window playing a simple scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look through the example_scenes to see examples of library syntax, animation types and object types. Use the 3b1b/videos repo for real video code but be aware older video code may not be compatible with the current manim version.

rubrics_metrics.name: CLI usage and useful flags
rubrics_metrics.description: When running in the CLI, some useful flags include: -w to write the scene to a file; -o to write the scene to a file and open the result; -s to skip to the end and just show the final frame; -so will save the final frame to an image and show it; -n <number> to skip ahead to the n'th animation of a scene; -f to make the playback window fullscreen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these flags to control rendering/output behavior during development and testing. Combine flags as needed (e.g., -o with -w). Consult the examples for typical usage patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: custom_config.yml for customization
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a look at custom_config.yml for further configuration. To add your customization, you can either edit this file, or add another file by the same name "custom_config.yml" to whatever directory you are running manim from.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use custom_config.yml to specify where videos should be output, where manim should look for image files and sounds, and other defaults regarding style and video quality. Example config for 3Blue1Brown videos is provided for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and community resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation is in progress at 3b1b.github.io/manim. And there is also a Chinese version maintained by @manim-kindergarten: docs.manim.org.cn. manim-kindergarten wrote and collected some useful extra classes and some codes of videos in manim_sandbox repo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the official docs and community-maintained resources for API details, extra utilities, and platform-specific instructions. Community repos may include extras not present in this repo; verify compatibility with your manim version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributing etiquette and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributing is always welcome. As mentioned above, the community edition has the most active ecosystem for contributions, with testing and continuous integration, but pull requests are welcome here too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting a pull request, explain the motivation for a given change and provide examples of its effect. Prefer community-edition if you want quicker response and CI/testing, but PRs to this repo are accepted if well motivated.
